source_text: Si non attingit manus eius ad ovem, duos turtures. Deus onera temperat. Pauperum munera non spernit.
thought_title: God adjusts the burden and accepts the poor's gifts
orientation: Origen is commenting on Leviticus 5:7, where the law allows a poor person to offer two turtledoves instead of a sheep for a sin offering.
pass_a_gloss: If [it] does not reach [the] hand of him to [the] sheep, two turtledoves. God [the] burdens tempers. [The] of [the] poor gifts not [he] scorns.

choices.term: Si non attingit manus eius ad ovem
choices.english: If his hand does not reach to a sheep
choices.why: Keeps the literal physical image of the hand reaching, which Origen uses to describe the poor person's inability to afford the sheep.
rejected: If he cannot afford a sheep
If his hand is not enough for a sheep

choices.why: Plain literal rendering of the pair of birds prescribed in Leviticus 5:7.
Preserves the active verb 'temperat' and the plural 'onera', showing God as the one who adjusts the weight of the law's demands.

choices.english: He does not scorn the gifts of the poor
choices.why: Keeps the negative verb 'non spernit' and the genitive plural 'pauperum', matching the source's compactness.
rejected: He does not reject the offerings of the poor
The gifts of the poor are not despised

bible_refs.note: Si non attingit manus eius ad ovem, duos turtures

pass_b_english: If his hand does not reach to a sheep, two turtledoves. God tempers burdens. He does not scorn the gifts of the poor.
